A clutter reduction effect using adaptive beam forming can be obtained uniformly across the entire ultrasonic image. This makes it possible to improve image quality not only in limited regions, but throughout the full imaging area.

The technique remains effective even when the number of bundled signals varies significantly from one region of the ultrasonic image to another. In conventional processing, variations in the number of received signals used for beam forming may cause uneven clutter suppression or inconsistent image quality. By contrast, this approach maintains stable performance despite such variations.

A received signal processing unit is provided to perform this operation. The unit includes a summing unit configured to bundle a plurality of received signals, or signals obtained by processing those received signals, for a predetermined imaging point. These bundled signals are then used to generate image information corresponding to that point.

The received signal processing unit also includes a weighting unit. The weighting unit calculates a coherence value representing the degree of coherence among the summed or bundled signals. Based on this coherence value, the weighting unit applies an appropriate weight to the signals. The weighting may be applied either before the summing operation or after the summing operation, depending on the configuration of the system.

In addition, the weighting unit performs nonlinear weighting of the coherence value in a predetermined direction within the subject. By emphasizing or suppressing the coherence value in this manner, the system improves the accuracy and effectiveness of signal weighting. As a result, clutter components can be reduced more reliably, and a clearer ultrasonic image can be produced across the entire imaging region.
outputs.L4:
The described ultrasonic imaging method is designed to reduce clutter uniformly across an entire ultrasound image by using adaptive beamforming techniques. In conventional ultrasonic imaging, clutter suppression can vary depending on the region of the image, especially when the number of received or bundled signals differs significantly from one location to another. This variation can lead to uneven image quality, with some areas appearing clearer than others. The proposed method addresses this problem by adapting the beamforming process so that clutter reduction remains consistent, even under conditions where signal density or bundling changes greatly across the imaging field.

To achieve this, the method evaluates the coherence of received ultrasonic signals. Signal coherence indicates how closely the received signals are related to one another and whether they likely originate from the intended imaging direction or from unwanted scattering, noise, or off-axis reflections. By analyzing this coherence information, the system can distinguish more effectively between useful image signals and clutter components. Signals that show strong directional consistency are treated as more reliable, while signals that appear incoherent or directionally inconsistent are suppressed.

The method further applies nonlinear weighting based on signal direction. Instead of treating all received signals equally, the beamformer assigns weights according to how well each signal aligns with the desired imaging direction. The nonlinear nature of the weighting allows the system to more strongly emphasize coherent, properly directed signals while more aggressively reducing contributions from clutter or off-axis interference. This helps prevent weak clutter from accumulating in the final image and improves the visibility of meaningful anatomical or structural features.

A key advantage of this approach is that it maintains stable clutter suppression even when the number of bundled signals changes substantially. In many ultrasonic imaging systems, differences in the number of signals used for beamforming can affect the strength of clutter reduction, producing inconsistent results across the image. By incorporating coherence calculation and adaptive nonlinear directional weighting, the proposed method compensates for these variations and produces a more uniform imaging result.

Overall, the technique improves ultrasonic image quality by enhancing contrast, reducing background clutter, and preserving useful signal information. It provides a more consistent and reliable beamforming process, making it especially valuable for applications where image uniformity and accurate visualization are important.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called a definite article, which means it points to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, when we say “the book,” we are not talking about just any book, but a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

Although “the” may seem simple, it helps make sentences clearer and more precise. It can turn a general idea into something specific: “a house” could be any house, but “the house” refers to one particular house. This small word gives meaning, direction, and context to what we say.

“The” is also used in many familiar phrases, titles, and names, such as “the sun,” “the world,” “the future,” and “the truth.” In each case, it gives importance to the noun that follows. Because it appears so often, many people hardly notice it, but without “the,” English would sound incomplete and less natural.

In short, “the” may be a tiny word, but it has a big purpose. It helps us be specific, connects ideas, and makes language easier to understand.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an ultrasound imaging invention that reduces clutter using adaptive beamforming and nonlinear coherence weighting across the image.
counterfactuals.output: An ultrasound imaging system and method are provided for reducing clutter in ultrasound images. Echo data received from a transducer array are beamformed using an adaptive beamformer that varies receive apodization, delay, or covariance-based weighting in response to local signal conditions. For each image location, a coherence measure is determined from the received channel data or beamformed sub-aperture data, and a nonlinear coherence weight is generated as a nonlinear function of the coherence measure. The nonlinear coherence weight is applied across a plurality of image samples to suppress incoherent or weakly coherent clutter while preserving highly coherent tissue and flow signals. In some embodiments, the adaptive beamforming and nonlinear coherence weighting are spatially varied over the image based on depth, aperture, signal-to-noise ratio, or local image statistics. The resulting image data are displayed with improved contrast, reduced sidelobe and reverberation artifacts, and enhanced delineation of anatomical structures.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, a received signal processing unit for an ultrasonic diagnostic apparatus that sums bundled received signals and applies weights based on coherence values.
counterfactuals.output:
A received signal processing unit for an ultrasonic diagnostic apparatus is configured to process a plurality of received signals obtained by receiving ultrasonic echoes with a plurality of transducer elements. The received signal processing unit comprises a bundling section configured to group the plurality of received signals into a plurality of signal bundles, each signal bundle including two or more received signals corresponding to respective reception channels; a summing section configured to generate a plurality of bundled sum signals by summing the received signals included in each of the plurality of signal bundles; a coherence-value calculating section configured to calculate, for each of the plurality of signal bundles, a coherence value indicative of a degree of similarity, phase alignment, correlation, or consistency among the received signals included in the corresponding signal bundle or between bundled sum signals; and a weighting section configured to apply, to each bundled sum signal, a weight determined in accordance with the coherence value associated with the corresponding signal bundle.

The received signal processing unit may further comprise an output section configured to generate a processed reception signal by combining the weighted bundled sum signals. The coherence value may be calculated on the basis of at least one of a phase difference, an amplitude correlation, a normalized cross-correlation value, a covariance value, a coherence factor, or a spatial coherence value among the received signals. The weighting section may be configured to increase a contribution of a bundled sum signal having a relatively high coherence value and to decrease a contribution of a bundled sum signal having a relatively low coherence value, thereby suppressing incoherent components including noise, sidelobe components, clutter, or off-axis echo components.

In one embodiment, the received signal processing unit includes delay circuitry configured to apply reception delay processing to the plurality of received signals prior to summation by the summing section. The bundling section may divide the reception channels into adjacent channel groups, partially overlapping channel groups, or non-overlapping channel groups. The coherence-value calculating section may calculate the coherence value for each group after the delay processing, and the weighting section may multiply each bundled sum signal by a corresponding weighting coefficient derived from the coherence value.

Accordingly, the received signal processing unit is capable of forming an ultrasonic reception signal in which signal components having high spatial or temporal coherence are emphasized while signal components having low coherence are attenuated, thereby improving image quality, contrast, and resolution in ultrasonic diagnostic imaging.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an abstract for a medical ultrasound signal processing invention involving a summing unit, a weighting unit, coherence calculation, and nonlinear weighting of summed or pre-summed received signals.
counterfactuals.output: An ultrasound signal processing apparatus and method are disclosed for improving image quality by adaptively weighting received echo signals based on spatial or temporal coherence. The apparatus includes a summing unit configured to generate a summed signal from a plurality of received ultrasound signals acquired by multiple transducer elements, and a coherence calculation unit configured to determine a coherence value representative of similarity among the received signals, pre-summed signals, or channel groups. A weighting unit applies a nonlinear weighting function to the summed signal and/or to one or more pre-summed received signals based on the calculated coherence value. The nonlinear weighting may suppress incoherent noise, clutter, sidelobe artifacts, or reverberation components while preserving coherent echo information associated with anatomical structures or flow. In some embodiments, the coherence value is calculated from phase, amplitude, correlation, sign, covariance, short-lag spatial coherence, or combinations thereof. The weighted signals may be further beamformed, envelope detected, filtered, or converted into ultrasound image data. The invention enables enhanced contrast, improved resolution, and reduced artifacts in medical ultrasound imaging without requiring substantial changes to the transducer array or acquisition sequence.
